Booking through three tech cycles: web, smartphone, AI

BKNG-tech-cycles-2026-10-14 · USD · series 2026-10-14T22:30:00Z · built 2026-10-15 00:06 UTC

Booking has met a new gatekeeper twice before. Each time it paid the gatekeeper, bought or built its own version of the new channel, spent on its own brand, and pulled travelers back to its own site and app.

AI assistants are the third gatekeeper. Booking is running the same moves again, in months rather than years. What is new is that the assistant can keep the checkout: in Google's AI Mode the traveler books without leaving Google (S23).

Three cycles on one clock

The playbook, cycle by cycle

Web and search. When Google began building hotel search, management said it was "principally based on content that Google receives, mostly from intermediaries, online travel agents" (call for the third quarter of 2011, S1). Booking kept paying for search, then bought KAYAK, the price-comparison site, for 1.8 billion dollars (S10). Afterwards it credited "increased advertising on KAYAK and effective offline advertising" (fourth quarter of 2013, S1).

Smartphone. This was the slow one. The goal came six years after the iPhone: "to try to get real estate on people's smartphones, so that they will come back directly to our brands" (third quarter of 2013, S1). Paid app installs were kept small because they "don't tend to be very economic" (second quarter of 2015, S1). Brand marketing was meant "to not only increase our share of direct traffic, but also enhance our effectiveness in the pay channels" (fourth quarter of 2017, S1).

AI assistants. Large language models (LLMs, the engines behind ChatGPT) came up on the call five months after ChatGPT launched (first quarter of 2023, S1). Booking was "one of the first wave of apps available in OpenAI's ChatGPT App Store" (Glenn Fogel, chief executive, third quarter of 2025, S1). It is paying the new gatekeeper too: "we are part of the test group of OpenAI for CPC," meaning cost per click, while staying "focused on keeping the direct traffic to us" (Ewout Steenbergen, finance chief, second quarter of 2026, S1).

Side by side

Web and search (2005–2014)Smartphone (2007–2019)AI assistants (2022–now)
The gatekeeperGoogle search, then price-comparison sitesSmall screens and app stores; Google adds a fourth mobile ad (2016, S1)ChatGPT, Google AI Mode
Pay itAdvertising from 89 million to 2.6 billion dollars (S25, S5)Kept buying mobile search; few paid installsLaunch partner for OpenAI and Google; paid-click test with OpenAI
Build or buyAgoda (S9), KAYAK (S10), OpenTable (S11), momondo (S12)Own apps, Genius loyalty, brand advertisingAI Trip Planner, own agent tools (S18, S21)
Pull directBooking.com brandDirect about half of room nights by 2018Stated goal; direct share flat since 2025
Time to first response1.3 years3.6 yearsUnder half a year
Who owns the checkoutBookingBooking (its app)Can be the assistant (S23)
Advertising per booking dollar4.0 cents (2005) to 5.2 cents (2014)5.6 cents (2017) to 4.4 cents (2025)4.4 cents (2024 and 2025)
